about: Living Knowledge claims: each says what kind of statement it is (status), what it is about (outcome) and the exact words in a source it rests on (terms).

records.text: The Churu plan describes loose-fitting, breathable cotton garments in light shades as traditional dress for heat in Rajasthan.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, section 2.3.3, p. 15

records.text: In a survey of 320 construction and welding workers in Bangladesh, wearing loose clothing was one of the adaptive behaviours examined; construction workers were more likely to report increasing it.
WHO advises light and loose-fitting clothing and bed linens in hot weather.
terms: Use light and loose-fitting clothing and bed linens
records.locator: WHO fact sheet, "What actions should the public take?"

records.text: UNICEF advises light and loose clothes and calls cotton ideal on hot days.
The Churu plan names lehariya turbans and odhnis among garments that allow airflow while shielding from the sun.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, section 2.3.3, p. 15

records.text: The plan states that layered clothing protects against heat by insulating against hot air; this is the plan's statement, not a measured result.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, section 2.3.3, p. 15
records.restriction: Not used as advice: untested, and may not hold in humid heat.

records.text: Older participants recalled kutcha houses with mud and hay roofs that kept the house cooler than outside, and contrasted them with tin-sheet roofs.
Participants described thatched roofs and additional windows as housing adaptations to heat.
Participants described coating the roof with limestone or alum to keep the house cool.
terms: coat the roof with limestone or alum

records.text: Lime plaster and Dulmera sandstone feature in older Bikaner buildings; the study reports its results only as preliminary findings.
The Churu plan encourages lime-plastered surfaces, jaali, courtyards, thick mud walls and high ceilings in new construction and retrofits, assigned to the Municipal Council Churu.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, table 4, measure 2

records.text: Some respondents hang wet sacks or cloths over the doors and windows to prevent hot air entering the house.
terms: wet sacks or cloths over the doors and windows

records.text: The same villages hire water tankers in summer because piped supply is irregular.
Participants cook very early in the morning and in the evening to keep kitchen heat out of the house during hotter hours.
terms: We cook food very early in the morning

records.text: WHO notes that gender shapes heat exposure, for example where women are primarily responsible for cooking indoors during hot weather.
terms: women are primarily responsible for cooking indoors

records.text: The Bikaner study says older buildings within the walled city, with narrow streets, internal courtyards and dense fabric, improve passive cooling through reciprocal shadowing; it reports this as preliminary findings without measurements.
The Churu plan describes traditional architecture in Rajasthan, including jaali, courtyards and lime plaster, and includes it as a planned measure.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, section 2.3.3 and table 4

records.text: Over a six-month duration, the air-well air temperature ranged from 27.48 °C to 30.92 °C in a single-storey terraced house in Malaysia.

quant.setting: One air well in one house

records.text: The authors conclude the minimum 10% openings rule is less effective than intended for thermal comfort.
The study found the double-heightened mud home more pleasant in thermal comfort factors and residents' responses than single-height mud and corrugated iron sheet houses.
In one vernacular stilt house in Palu City, the outdoor air temperature peaked at 36.8 °C while the first-floor indoor peak reached 32 °C.
terms: indoor peak temperature on the 1st floor reached 32

quant.comparator: Outdoor air at the same site
quant.period: Measurement period not stated in the abstract

records.text: Measurements in a Simalungun traditional house were compared with simulation in a building tool.
The study investigated the thermal performance of vernacular courtyard houses in Jaffna, comparing two houses.
records.note: The abstract does not state whether performance was measured or simulated.

records.text: Researchers observed water pots for drinking in front of most houses, accessible to everyone.
terms: Water pots for drinking in front of most houses

records.text: The Churu plan proposes distributing cool clay refrigerators and water pots to low-income groups and filling community matkas at bus stops, hospitals and markets.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, table 4, measures 2 and 5

records.text: A livestock study describes keeping drinking water in an earthen pot to cool it in summer as a traditional village practice in India.
Carrying water bottles covered by wet jute was observed as a common practice during travel and at work.
records.locator: Results, theme 3, vocational and transport adjustments

records.text: Cool drinking water from public taps was among participants' preferred coping mechanisms in Dalkhola, West Bengal.
terms: Cool drinking water from public taps

records.text: The Churu plan proposes filling community matkas at key locations.
records.locator: Churu Heat Action Plan, table 4, measure 5

records.text: Participants described preferring buttermilk and curd in summer and using desert beans in dishes such as ker sangri.
Fruit was preferred in summer, but many respondents said it is not affordable.
Some participants soak screw pine flowers in stored water, believing it cools the body; no evidence of an effect is offered.
records.restriction: A cultural belief, documented without effect claims.

records.text: Participants described applying multani mitti (bentonite clay) to the body and using tamarind water for heat symptoms.
The authors state there is no scientific evidence supporting the spice decoction's effectiveness.
terms: no scientific evidence supporting its effectiveness

records.text: Key informants said scheme working hours are adjusted in summer, for example from 9 am to 5 pm to 6 am to 11 am or 12 pm, when a heatwave alert is received.
records.locator: Results, theme 3, vocational and transport adjustments

records.text: Participants described sickness absence and loss of wages in extreme heat, making it hard for daily-wage workers to make ends meet.
Planning work during cooler hours was among the adaptive behaviours examined among construction and welding workers in Bangladesh.
Older informal workers in Dhaka use altered work schedules and traditional cooling practices, but these were largely insufficient given socioeconomic constraints.
terms: altered work schedules and traditional cooling practices

records.text: WHO advises avoiding going outside and strenuous activity during the hottest time of day.
terms: Avoid going outside and doing strenuous activity during the hottest time of day

records.text: Construction workers in Bangladesh were more likely to report increasing regular breaks (OR 9.49).
A pilot study of 416 informal workers in Dhaka recommends rest breaks and hydration access.
A village council head described an informal group called Sajag used to disseminate weather and heat information and to adjust scheme working hours.
Trees were seen as the primary coping strategy for heat stress in Dalkhola, though many participants noted a loss of tree cover.
terms: Trees were seen as the primary coping strategy

records.text: Researchers observed that almost all households had huge trees in their setbacks, offering shade.
Temples at Angkor with less tree canopy cover were warmer at night than the surrounding forest.
terms: warmer at night than the surrounding forest

records.text: The World Bank recommends promoting urban greening through strategic planning.
terms: promote urban greening through strategic planning

records.text: Across 20 pairs of parallel sites in Singapore, street shade lowered air temperature by an average of 0.8 °C and lowered mean radiant temperature markedly.
The World Bank lists cooling city spaces through wind, shade and urban design among its options for action.
terms: cool city spaces through wind, shade, and urban design

records.text: A systematic review found that in some settings health care providers and relatives continue to advise water supplementation in hot weather, and concludes that exclusive breastfeeding is recommended even in hot conditions.
terms: exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) is recommended even in hot conditions

records.text: UNICEF advises breastfeeding infants under 6 months exclusively in heat waves.
Participants described constructing chappra (animal sheds made of straw) and spraying water to cool animals.
In a controlled comparison, an open-ridge ventilated, double-slope thatch roof shed created a more favourable microclimate than an asbestos roof shed and reduced the heat-related drop in milk yield.
terms: open-ridge ventilated, double-slope thatch roof shed

records.text: Avishaan rams under heat stress given earthen pot water lost less body weight and had higher intake than heat-stressed rams given ambient water.
